transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-09 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Connor Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (Aperture Head of ML), Ethan Cole (Platform Eng), Laura Sato (CTO)

Summary:
Aperture Labs is exploring moving portions of their LLM workload off a managed provider and into either Redwood Hosted for quick wins, or Redwood Dedicated / Private for regulated, sensitive data. Main concerns are eval parity with their existing TGI/vLLM stack, on-prem networking/KMS needs, and latency vs cost trade-offs for high-throughput summarization and retrieval-augmented generation.

Topics covered:
- Current stack (Anthropic + TGI they host) and pain points
- Requirement for private deployment (air-gapped option) and KMS/HSM integration
- Model compatibility and eval parity: vLLM/TGI -> Redwood runtime mapping
- Benchmarks needed: latency p95, tokens/sec, memory per-stream, batch sizing
- Operational features: canary rollouts, KV cache behavior, burst autoscaling
- Compliance: SOC2, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, data residency

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick round robin?
[00:08] Priya Raman: yeah hi, i'm priya, we run the ml org at aperture. we own the models, mainly run tgi internally with vllm as the runtime for inference.
[00:18] Ethan Cole: ethan here, platform eng, i'll own the network and deploy side.
[00:22] Laura Sato: laura, cto, i'll pop in and out but overall want to see where security lands.
[00:28] Maya Chen: awesome. Connor, you want to quick intro?
[00:31] Connor Diaz: sure, i'm connor, infra se, i look after perf and model onboarding at redwood — mostly focused on quantization, batching, and kv cache behavior.
[00:40] Priya Raman: quick context, we've been on a hybrid approach. for public facing stuff we used openai, for internal higher-sensitivity we run tgi on prem with vllm. main pain is cost and operational overhead when scaling to bursts. also, small but important, our devs want parity: model outputs must match closely or we need a retrain.
[01:04] Maya Chen: totally. when you say parity, do you mean identical logits / token choices or acceptable quality with same prompts?
[01:11] Priya Raman: acceptable quality but no regressions on our eval sets — which are mainly long doc summarization and multi-turn chat for internal search. we have ~200 prompt/eval suites.
[01:21] Connor Diaz: okay good, so we'll run your evals against our hosted model and a dedicated private deployment if needed. one thing to flag: vllm uses an execution path that can differ with kernel choices; we map those at the compilation layer — for Redwood we pick kernels based on sequence length and quantization profile, so sometimes you'll see subtle differences in tokens.
[01:45] Ethan Cole: specifics on networking — for private we need to keep traffic inside our VPC, bring-your-own-KMS (we use an HSM via vendor), and ideally an air-gap option for a few PII datasets. is that supported?
[01:56] Maya Chen: yes, our Redwood Private supports customer-managed networking, KMS integrations, and we offer an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. we'll send the architecture checklist.
[02:07] Laura Sato: and audit logs? we need immutable audit trails for model access for compliance audits.
[02:13] Connor Diaz: yes, audit logs with per-token traceability are possible, and we can integrate with your SIEM. slight caveat — retention windows are configurable but larger retention is a paid add-on.
[02:25] Priya Raman: perf question: our p95 latency requirement for interactive summarization is <= 450ms for sequences ~512 tokens. can you meet that on dedicated or hosted?
[02:36] Connor Diaz: depends on the model and batch policy. for 13B class models quantized and pinned to dedicated GPUs we hit ~200-350ms p95 for single-stream low-batch; hosted can hit similar numbers with burst capacity but you'd want dedicated for tighter SLOs. we'll need to run your exact prompts through our harness.
[02:56] Ethan Cole: what's the overhead to spin up dedicated capacity — and can we do canary deploys?
[03:03] Maya Chen: dedicated is reserved pools, we support canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback to a cheaper variant. onboarding timeline is typically 4-8 weeks for reserved capacity plus any private networking work.
[03:16] Priya Raman: one blocker is model artifacts — we package models as usual. how's support for custom ops or patched tch kernels that we currently use in our vllm builds?
[03:29] Connor Diaz: custom ops are trickier in hosted — we generally bring models through standard formats (ggml, Transformers weights, ONNX for some). for Private on-prem we can accommodate more custom builds; it becomes an engineering scoping item. we'll want to review any patched kernels.
[03:45] Priya Raman: hmm, so for parity we may need to keep some custom ops; can we run our vllm stack side-by-side and compare?
[03:51] Connor Diaz: yes, that's the plan — we'll run bench comparisons: your vllm baseline vs Redwood Private and Redwood Dedicated. we'll log token-level diffs and produce a regression report.
[04:02] Maya Chen: also want to call out cost levers: batching size, kv caching, and quantization profile. often teams are surprised by cache hit rates changing apparent latency.
[04:14] Ethan Cole: speaking of kv cache, how do you handle long session state for multi-turn? we need persisted kv for sessions up to 100k tokens.
[04:23] Connor Diaz: we support K-V caching with spill-to-disk and incremental restore. for ultra-long sessions we recommend a tiered approach; that will be part of the tuning during the bench runs.
[04:33] Priya Raman: security nuance — we need SSO (SAML) and RBAC mapping to our AD. also encryption in transit and at rest with our KMS.
[04:43] Maya Chen: Redwood supports SAML SSO and RBAC, and for Private we integrate your KMS. we'll include the SSO mapping doc.
[04:50] Laura Sato: any current customers running air-gapped deployments?
[04:54] Connor Diaz: yes, a couple in healthcare — we can anonymize references and set up a call for deeper ops questions.
[04:59] Priya Raman: great. about model updates / rollouts — we need fine-grained control, canary percentages, immediate rollback, and a way to pin old model versions for compliance reproduction.
[05:10] Connor Diaz: we have model version pinning and can do staged rollouts with automatic rollback on regression signals tied to your eval suite.
[05:18] Maya Chen: sounds like actionables. we'll run a bench with your 200 eval prompts. Connor will instrument the harness to capture p95, p50, tokens/sec, and token-level diffs.
[05:27] Priya Raman: that's perfect. also can you share an initial cost estimate for hosted vs dedicated vs private? approximate run cost per million tokens and infra delta for dedicated.
[05:38] Maya Chen: yes, i'll include delta estimates with assumptions about batch size and hit rates.
[05:44] Ethan Cole: question on integration: do you provide terraform modules or helm charts for private deploy?
[05:49] Connor Diaz: we have terraform + helm chart examples for private deployment and VPC setup; for air-gapped we provide an offline installer and ops runbook.
[05:58] Priya Raman: any surprises we should watch out for moving from vllm/tgi? like differences in generation stemming from tokenization or detokenization?
[06:07] Connor Diaz: tokenization differences can happen — we normalize on model tokenizer and we'll run a tokenizer-consistency check as part of the eval. detokenization differences are rare but will show up in token-level diffs.
[06:18] Maya Chen: ok briefly, timeline options: 1) quick POC on Redwood Hosted to validate eval parity (~1-2 weeks), 2) dedicated reserved pool for production parity (~4-8 weeks), 3) private/on-prem for regulated datasets (~6-12 weeks).
[06:33] Priya Raman: we're leaning to do a two-track approach: quick hosted POC while connor scopes private deployment requirements.
[06:41] Connor Diaz: sounds good. for the hosted POC we'll need credentials and access to your eval harness or a sample payloads set.
[06:48] Priya Raman: we'll provide a redacted eval set and a s3 bucket with sample docs — I'll coordinate with ethan.
[06:55] Ethan Cole: ok i will provision a bucket and shared creds (read-only) and send to maya.
[06:59] Maya Chen: perfect. any other questions?
[07:03] Laura Sato: just on contracts / procurement — what's the process if we want to go dedicated after POC?
[07:08] Maya Chen: typically we convert POC usage to committed capacity. sales will work with you on contract and procurement; we can align timelines to your fiscal quarter.
[07:15] Priya Raman: thanks, that's helpful.

[07:20] Final recap by Maya:
- Redwood to run POC on Hosted with Aperture evals (Maya/Connor)
- Connor to set up benchmark harness and mapping notes for vLLM/TGI differences
- Security docs and private checklist to be sent by Maya
- Aperture to share evals and dataset sensitivity matrix (Priya/Ethan)
- Schedule technical bench run (week of 2027-08-23)

[07:40] Meeting end.
